messages.subject: Losing my ,core.cdf designation
parts:
Hi, I'm having a strange problem with my 'ExonRmaPlm' object.

Short Version: even though I have set the cdf of my original Cel set to
be the ,core.cdf, I have lost it along the way (seems at the quantile
normalization part, see below). The strange thing is that at some point
it worked, and now it doesn't. I don't know if I'm reinitializing my
variables incorrectly, or what.

Longer version: So originally everything I had tried was working after
the initial sorting out the bugs. Then at various points I updated to
have the bugs fixed (e.g. get the 'Merged' tags, etc). So I reran a
number of analysis (i.e. completely wiped out the plm fit from before
and redid it with new programs). I had some problems where I was getting
Inf residuals, etc. and weird errors, but somehow (probably by erasing
and starting over at some level) everything went through. I thought at
the time most of this was caused by 'left-over' files from previous runs
that were error-ridden, but I mention it just in case. Unfortunately, I
don't know what I did nor what was the magic part of that combination,
but at some point everything ran through, I had chip and probe effects
and residuals, and when I called readUnits, everything came up naturally
(i.e. a unit was calling up a transcript cluster at all levels). Since
then, I have wiped everything out of my R session (I was getting a huge
.RData file and I couldn't figure out from where) and when I
reinitialized my variables, everything is working at the unit=probeset
level and nothing has the right .cdf associated with it after the first
step. Moreover, when I try to find my probe effects they are all 0,
probably because its cdf file is wrong so it can't find the data?
Calling up the chip effects, however, gives the exact same thing as it
did before and it's cdf file is ",core,monocell.cdf" like it should be.
So my actual files seem to be the same (i.e. I didn't rerun the plm at
some point and forget that I had done so). I don't know if I've done
something wrong nor if this is related to my earlier problems when
trying to run the residuals.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

My sequence of code:
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2" cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name,
chipType=chipType)
coreChipType <- paste(chipType, "core", sep=",")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(coreChipType)
setCdf(cs, cdf)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN<-getOutputDataSet(qn)
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
pb<-getProbeAffinityFile(plm)

readUnits(pb,units=1)

parts: Hi.

On 2/27/07, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi, I'm having a strange problem with my 'ExonRmaPlm' object.
>
> Short Version: even though I have set the cdf of my original Cel set to
> be the ,core.cdf, I have lost it along the way (seems at the quantile
> normalization part, see below). The strange thing is that at some point
> it worked, and now it doesn't. I don't know if I'm reinitializing my
> variables incorrectly, or what.

So, getCdf(cs) gives you the "core" CDF, but getCdf(plm) doesn't.
What does getCdf(csN) on the CEL set in between give? This will help
me troubleshoot.

BTW/FYI, the QuantileNormalizer keeps the chip type of the input CEL
files and do not update it to the chip type of the CDF set by
setCdf(cs, cdf). This is due to the way QN is implemented (copying
source CEL file and then update its data; the chip type is in the CEL
header and that does not get updated), and not due to an explicit
design strategy. I never though about changing the CDF before the QN
but only directly before the PLM, so I did not think of this scenario.
It should only make a difference to the QN if QN is done on PMs or
MMs only and if these are different in the new CDF. I will put it on
the to do list of updates, but it is not on the urgent list since in
most case it is sufficient to do setCdf(csN, cdf).

A possible reason for your problem (the bug?) may be that the core CDF
is carried through when the analysis is done the first time, but if
restarted and parts are already fitted, this somehow fails. If so, it
is a bug and will be fixed.

>
> Longer version: So originally everything I had tried was working after
> the initial sorting out the bugs. Then at various points I updated to
> have the bugs fixed (e.g. get the 'Merged' tags, etc). So I reran a

> don't know what I did nor what was the magic part of that combination,

You could use something like

logFile <- sprintf("%s.log", dataSetName);
log <- Verbose(logFile, threshold=-4, removeFile=FALSE);
timestampOn(log);

and pass this to your method calls via argument 'verbose', e.g.

fit(plm, verbose=log)

and you should now get a log file written.

(Footnote: It is on my wish list to have an automatic file logging
mechanism that always log to file, but other things are more
prioritized.)

> but at some point everything ran through, I had chip and probe effects
> and residuals, and when I called readUnits, everything came up naturally
> (i.e. a unit was calling up a transcript cluster at all levels). Since
> then, I have wiped everything out of my R session (I was getting a huge
> .RData file and I couldn't figure out from where) and when I
> reinitialized my variables, everything is working at the unit=probeset
> level and nothing has the right .cdf associated with it after the first
> step. Moreover, when I try to find my probe effects they are all 0,
> probably because its cdf file is wrong so it can't find the data?
Sound like a reasonable explanation.

> Calling up the chip effects, however, gives the exact same thing as it
> did before and it's cdf file is ",core,monocell.cdf" like it should be.

The chip effect CEL files, named *,chipEffects.cel, are created from
scratch, meaning their CEL headers are written by aroma.affymetrix
(and not copied from another CEL file). Thus, the chip type of the
input data set is inherited and turned into a "monocell" chip type,
i.e. "*,core,monocell", and is *written* to the CEL file.

This is likely reason why you don't have problems with the chip effect
files, but you still see it in the quantile normalized CEL files.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: Losing my ,core.cdf designation
parts: Hi guys,

> My sequence of code:
> chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2" cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name,
> chipType=chipType)
> coreChipType <- paste(chipType, "core", sep=",")
> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(coreChipType)
> setCdf(cs, cdf)
> qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, typesToUpdate="pm")
> csN<-getOutputDataSet(qn)

> plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
> chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
> pb<-getProbeAffinityFile(plm)

I just did a little test run (with 6 HuEx arrays) and it seemed to work OK. I
think the key is this: if I create csN via

csN <- process(qn)

rather than getOutputDataSet(), the cdf is preserved. This is because
process() calls normalizeQuantile.AffymetrixCelSet, where we do an explicit
setCdf() at the end to preserve the cdf. In fact I'm not entirely sure what
getOutputDataSet is supposed to do here, unless process() has been called
already. Am I missing something?

Cheers,

Ken

> csN <- process(qn)
>
> rather than getOutputDataSet(), the cdf is preserved. This is because
> process() calls normalizeQuantile.AffymetrixCelSet, where we do an explicit
> setCdf() at the end to preserve the cdf. In fact I'm not entirely sure what
> getOutputDataSet is supposed to do here, unless process() has been called
> already. Am I missing something?

Ok, this explains it. I've now fixed it so that both
getOutputDataSet() and process() is guaranteed to carry down the same
AffymetrixCdfFile object as set in the input data set. This will be
available in the next version. In the meantime, do the same manually:

setCdf(csN, getCdf(cs))

Details: When process() is called and the data has not yet been
normalized, the code that does the normalization (the function Ken
refers to above) does also make sure that the CDF is carried down.
When process() is called on data already normalized, that code is not
called, but instead just getOutputDataSet(). The getOutputDataSet()
method is where the problem was; it did not pass down the CDF. So,
the fix was simple. BTW, since getOutputDataSet() is define in
superclass Transform, this fix should apply to all transformation
(calibration, normalization, ...) methods inheriting from Transform.

Cheers

Henrik


>
> Cheers,
>
> Ken
